<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard Arch User Repository package definition. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources the file at the top level and prints metadata — it does not execute `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. 

The top-level code consists entirely of variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, url, license, provides, replaces, conflicts, depends, optdepends) and source array definitions. The source URLs point to the package's own GitHub releases (`https://github.com/Revincx/Yurigram/releases/download/...`), which is the expected upstream source for this binary package. The sha256sums are present and populated with actual checksums (not SKIP).

There are no top-level command substitutions, no eval, no base64 decoding, no curl|bash or wget|bash patterns, and no data exfiltration code. The source arrays merely define download URLs as strings — they do not trigger any downloads or executions during the sourcing phase. The `package()` function, which contains the actual file installation logic, is not executed at this gate.

No genuinely malicious behavior is present in the top-level scope that would execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR PKGBUILD with no top-level malicious code
</summary>
</security_assessment>
